title: Final-Bill Desk Note: Vacancy Factor on Estimated Net Energy Metering Exports
content:
When the estimated period of a Net Energy Metering export credit ends in a final bill of the Electric Service Agreement hosting the system, a vacancy factor applies to the export estimate according to how far the final bill's usage has fallen.

**Rule.** When the estimated period's bill is a final bill and its billed kWh are below the low-use ratio of 0.50 multiplied by the billed kWh of the preceding period's bill, the vacancy factor is the empty-premises factor of 1.12. When it is a final bill and its billed kWh are at least that much, it is the partly-occupied factor of 1.05. On a regular bill no vacancy adjustment applies.

**Bills compared.** The estimated period's bill is the most recent service bill of the hosting Electric Service Agreement; its kind and its total billed kWh are printed on it. The preceding period's bill is the service bill whose billing period ends on the billing period end of the most recent export credit in the net metering history; its total billed kWh are compared.

## Vacancy factor

| Estimated period's bill | Billed kWh compared with 0.50 of the preceding bill's billed kWh | Vacancy factor |
|---|---|---|
| Final bill | Below | 1.12 |
| Final bill | Equal or above | 1.05 |
| Regular bill | Any | No vacancy adjustment |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical)

Hypothetical input: the preceding period's bill shows 800 kWh, so the comparison figure is 400 kWh.

- A final bill showing 399 kWh is below it: 1.12.
- A final bill showing exactly 400 kWh is not below it: 1.05.
- A regular bill showing 150 kWh: no vacancy adjustment.
